2. DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

DeepSeek has introduced a new search and fetch API priced at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests. This service allows developers to integrate real-time web retrieval directly into their applications.

My Take

DeepSeek is charging for search, proving once again that in the AI gold rush, the only people making money are the ones selling the shovels—or in this case, the slightly faster internet scrapers. At least the pricing is transparent, which is more than I can say for the average AI startup's burn rate.

3. NY announces game ownership bill requiring ownership rather than licensing

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

A new bill introduced in New York aims to mandate that digital games be sold as owned property rather than licensed software. The legislation would also require publishers to ensure games remain functional after official support ends.

My Take

New York is finally telling game publishers that 'you own nothing and you'll be happy' isn't a business model, it's a hostage situation. If this passes, publishers might actually have to stop treating customers like monthly subscribers to a digital paperweight. It’s a bold move to suggest that if you pay $70 for a game, you should actually be allowed to play it in a decade.

Summary

Research published in Nature indicates that bleached corals can recover significantly faster when in physical contact with healthy neighboring corals. This finding provides new insights into coral reef resilience and potential conservation strategies.

My Take
